title: Deterministic profile publish pipeline for onboarding pinsets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: onboarding a model currently produces nondeterministic performance profiles because dataset sampling, prompt variant selection, and eval runner selection can vary between runs. That variability hinders reliable version pinning and confuses downstream customers and the Console (flaky performance deltas in release rollouts).

Goal: Build a deterministic, auditable pipeline that ties a model onboarding pinset (the set of model artifacts + metadata + semantic tags) to a single published performance profile artifact. This pipeline will: 1) freeze dataset sampling seeds and prompt variant weights, 2) lock eval-runner configuration and environment (docker image + binary sha), and 3) publish a signed, versioned profile artifact to the catalog with provenance metadata.

Scope: implement deterministic sampling and runner-selection glue in the benchmark harness, add a publication stage that emits a signed profile bundle (JSON+metadata), and expose small APIs for Console and the model catalog to fetch pinset -> profile mapping. This ticket focuses on harness-side changes (sampling, runner shims, artifact signing) and the publish contract; catalog/console integration will follow in a separate ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Given a model onboarding job with the same pinset and harness config, two independent runs must produce byte-identical profile bundles (excluding a monotonically increasing build_id field).
Profile bundles include: dataset signature (sha256), prompt-template hash, eval-runner image sha, deterministic seed list, and aggregated per-scenario latency and quality stats with sample counts.
Published profile bundles are signed with the internal key and stored in the profile-catalog bucket under /profiles/<model>/<version>/<publish-id>.json
Console API can resolve pinset -> publish-id via the new mapping endpoint (integration smoke test exists in postman/newman).
Telemetry shows stable variance reduction: standard deviation of throughput across two runs with identical pinset must be < 3% for the canonical suite.
tasks: Add deterministic sampler module to harness that accepts a seed list and emits identical sample slices
Create eval-runner manifest binder so runner image and args are recorded in artifact metadata
Implement profile bundler that consolidates stats + provenance and signs bundle
Add unit + e2e tests that run harness twice with identical config and assert byte-identical bundles
Document publish contract and provide example CLI invocation for release engineers
comments: 2025-02-11: Initial design review — PM (Lucas Meyer) requested explicit inclusion of runner image SHA and OS kernel info in provenance. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-02-15: Design iteration — switched from per-scenario random seed to per-dataset seed-list to cover distributed sampling edge cases (Riley).
2025-02-20: Engineering note — discovered nondeterminism from background shuffling in the preprocessor (ENG-14356). Added deterministic flag and patched preprocessor in harness core.
2025-02-25: PR opened (1423) with sampler + bundler implementation. Requested review from research and infra teams.
2025-03-02: Code review feedback (from Markus Chen) — reworked signing scheme to use KMS envelope with local ephemeral key; updated bundler to include signer metadata.
2025-03-04: Integration smoke test added: CLI publish -> catalog mapping created and verified in staging. Remaining: performance regression tests and Console integration ticket prep.
